title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) measuring whether placing a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification) we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents using gpt-5-mini and a canonical verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes and 72 model calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults: contingency counts n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0. The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). We report the full preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting (completed_episode_count = 144, model_calls_used = 72, failed_episode_count = 0), representative validator traces, exact inferential outputs, and artifact-grounded methodological recommendations to measure verifier utility under realistic error regimes (independent-generation arms, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored to translate high-level operator intents into low-level device configurations for network operations (NetOps). This intent→configuration capability could shorten change pipelines but raises operational risk: a generated configuration may violate reachability, security policy, or sequencing invariants and cause outages if applied without checks. A common mitigation proposal is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) stack in which stochastic generation is followed by deterministic verification and, when required, human review or automated repair. Prior empirical work documents promising intent→config accuracy in constrained settings [1] and prototype co-pilots that include verification components [2], but systematic preregistered experiments that couple generator outputs, deterministic verifiers, and emulator‑observed execution outcomes remain scarce [3].

We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 to isolate the verifier’s pure detection capability on identical generator outputs under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The formal research question is: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults when the same generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? By enforcing a single shared initial candidate per intent, the experiment measures only deterministic detection/prevention (and not benefits due to alternate sampling, generator re-invocation, or repair-mediated candidate replacement). Our contribution is an artifact-grounded, preregistered paired run (72 confirmatory pairs) that resulted in a ceiling/null outcome (no baseline faults), together with concrete, artifact-supported recommendations for follow-up confirmatory designs capable of measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven intent→configuration translation and NetOps co-pilots have rapidly evolved. Nguyen et al. present intent-based configuration generation in constrained vendor dialects and report emulator-based task accuracy [1]. Multi-agent and tool-augmented frameworks that target intent-driven NetOps have been proposed and prototyped; these systems commonly integrate validators to reduce regressions but rarely publish preregistered detection-evaluation against emulator-executed outcomes [2,4].

Generate–verify–repair and related architectures have precedent in code-generation and program-repair literature, where deterministic checkers and test suites validate stochastic outputs and guide repair loops; these precedents motivate similar stacks for NetOps but require domain-specific verification of protocol semantics and runtime execution effects [3]. Classical deterministic network verification techniques (header-space analyses, policy checkers, and reachability analyses) are logical verifier candidates because they encode precise forwarding- and policy-level invariants; integrating such tools into GVR stacks is an active area of system design and evaluation [5].

The present study positions a preregistered paired test—explicitly constrained to shared_initial_candidate semantics—within this literature. That isolation complements prior prototype studies by providing a clean inferential contrast: identical candidate executed with and without deterministic verification. Where prior reports argue architectural promise, our artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome highlights the practical consequence of low baseline error prevalence under constrained prompts and task banks and clarifies what confirmatory contracts are required to measure verifier detection utility experimentally.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The experiment was preregistered as c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 and the design and analysis plan were frozen before observing any outcomes. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the paired absolute change in undetected operational-fault proportion when the identical generated candidate is evaluated with a deterministic verifier (guarded) versus executed without verification (baseline). The confirmatory hypothesis H1 targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 with two‑sided alpha = 0.05 and power ≥ 0.80; the preregistered sample-size heuristic required ≈63 pairs and N = 72 pairs was adopted (stratified equally across three topology-difficulty strata) to provide margin for exclusions.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and experimental contract. Per the registered execution_contract and adapter semantics, each intent received exactly one initial LLM generation that was shared across the two paired conditions (baseline and guarded). Baseline: the shared candidate was executed in an isolated emulator and the resulting end-to-end emulator outcome (fault/no fault) was recorded. Guarded: the deterministic verifier deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") executed on the same candidate; if it flagged a violation, the guarded outcome was recorded as prevented (no emulator execution); if it did not flag, the identical candidate was executed. This strict shared_initial_candidate design isolates verifier detection capacity and prevents generator-sampling variability from contributing to paired discordance. The preregistration explicitly disallowed independent per-condition generation for the confirmatory arm; therefore the guarded arm could only alter outcomes by deterministic detection and prevention, not by producing alternative candidates.

Model, adapter, and verifier configuration. The declared generation model is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). The adapter family used was hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The archived model configuration records requested_model = "gpt-5-mini", provider = "openai_responses", max_output_tokens = 2000, and temperature = null (provider default sampling semantics; temperature recorded as null in the archived configuration indicates no explicit sampling parameter was set at generation time). The canonical verifier was deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements the pre-specified scoring_rule = "full_intent_constraint_validation" and produces per-episode structured validator_trace objects that include parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, validation_before/after final_state, violation_codes, and difficulty metadata.

Task-bank generation, contamination controls, and stratification. Tasks were created deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest entry encodes a natural-language intent, an explicitly enumerated required_sequence (ordered field changes), allowed_touched_fields, initial and expected final states, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard) with named patterns such as make_before_break and shutdown_configure_restore. The preregistration applied deterministic provenance and exact-match contamination checks against public corpora; exact matches would be excluded from the confirmatory set. The confirmatory sample executed as planned with no exclusions. Per the preregistration, the confirmatory N = 72 pairs were stratified equally across three topology-difficulty strata (planned 24 pairs per stratum) to support descriptive stratified analyses.

Execution protocol, retries and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two retried attempts for transient hosted-API errors; all retries and provider-call metadata were recorded. The execution manifest records completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72. Deterministic_reconciliation.json reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, cache_miss_count = 72, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 72}, consistent with one shared initial generation per pair. These deterministic accounting artifacts ensure the confirmatory contract semantics and provider-call budget were honored and are archived in the evidence bundle for reproducibility.
sections.results:
Execution and deterministic accounting. The run completed without technical failures. Key recorded artifacts: execution/raw_results.jsonl (input for analysis), execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", temperature = null), deterministic_reconciliation.json (provider-call audit), and analysis/condition_summary.csv. The manifest reports planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72.

Primary paired contingency and inferential outcomes. Aggregating the 72 preregistered pairs yields the paired contingency counts: n_11 = 72 (guarded=1, baseline=1), n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Per the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor, the paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. The exact McNemar two-sided test (pre-specified when discordant pairs exist) reports p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI was computed with bootstrap_seed = 1729 and bootstrap_resamples = 10000 and is [0.0, 0.0]. The per-condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) report baseline success_rate = 1.0 and guarded success_rate = 1.0.

Representative validator diagnostics. Representative scoring artifacts for sampled episodes (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json through task-000006-*.json) demonstrate consistent verifier behavior: parsed_command_count observed ranges were 2–6 across representative tasks, required_command_count equaled parsed or required counts per intent, difficulty.level fields included medium/hard/very_hard labels, validator_version = "5.0", score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION", and violation_count = 0 in these examples. The validator traces record the normalized_configuration and validation_before/after final_state mappings, confirming that the verifier parsed each shared candidate and produced a validity decision. These representative traces are archived and reproduce the per-episode validator outputs reported in the analysis artifacts.

Contamination, exclusions, and missingness. The archived analysis/contamination_summary.csv contains zero flagged exact-match contaminations for confirmatory pairs and analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 72 with no failed or unscorable episodes. Because there were no exclusions and no discordant outcomes, pre-specified sensitivity analyses (e.g., treating excluded pairs as failures) do not alter the degenerate numerical conclusion for the confirmatory estimand.
sections.discussion:
Inferential interpretation of the ceiling/null outcome. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate contract validly isolates deterministic verifier detection on identical generator outputs. Observing zero baseline faults therefore produces a ceiling effect: when the generator's shared candidates are uniformly valid in the emulator, a verifier that only detects violations on those identical candidates cannot improve executed outcomes. The recorded contingency (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0), paired difference = 0.0, McNemar p = 1.0, and bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0] are direct, artifact-grounded consequences of the preregistered contract and the observed data.

Design implications and actionable recommendations. The preregistered confirmatory contract intentionally excluded independent per-condition generation and repair-enabled flows; as a result the observed run cannot speak to verifier benefits that arise from repair or alternate-sample selection. To measure operational verifier utility in future confirmatory studies we recommend, and the archived evidence supports, at least three contract modifications: (1) independent-generation arms allowing separate generator calls per condition so that sampler variability and verifier-influenced candidate distributions can create discordance; (2) repair-enabled flows where the verifier, upon flagging, triggers a single controlled repair attempt (recorded and counted under the adapter's maximum_repair_calls budget) and the repaired candidate is executed end-to-end; (3) adversarial or fault-injection task banks intentionally increasing baseline error prevalence (sequencing violations, ambiguous intents, protocol edge cases) to expose true positives and false positives and permit estimation of detection rate and blocking cost tradeoffs. These recommendations are grounded in the experiment's execution manifest and analysis artifacts which demonstrate that the current contract was faithfully enforced and that the absence of baseline faults—not verifier ineffectiveness—explains the null result.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the single shared generation per intent and provider-default sampling (temperature = null) limit sensitivity to generator sampling effects; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null and the deterministic provider-call audit confirms one shared generation per pair. Construct validity: emulator-observed faults are a conservative proxy for operational harm but do not capture traffic-dependent timing interactions, mid‑flight state races, or vendor-specific runtime idiosyncrasies present in production hardware. External validity: the study used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), one deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a synthetic/emulated task bank; extrapolation to other models, vendor dialects, or production devices is not supported. Conclusion validity: because baseline error prevalence was zero in the preregistered task bank, the confirmatory design lacks power to demonstrate verifier benefit under the enforced contract. Finally, contamination controls flagged zero exact matches in analysis/contamination_summary.csv, but residual uncertainty remains because private model training data cannot be exhaustively proven absent.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen generator (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0, bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults, a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Demonstrating verifier operational utility will require confirmatory contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, or multi-model comparisons. All execution artifacts, validator traces, analysis logs, and preregistration materials cited in this paper are archived in the evidence bundle to support replication and targeted follow-on studies.

Models and tools: initial generation used gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json) orchestrated via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") served as the canonical verifier; an isolated emulator executed candidate configurations. Preregistration: study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 was preregistered and frozen before observing outcomes. Key archived artifacts: execution/raw_results.jsonl (input to analysis; SHA‑256 recorded in manifest), execution/model_configuration.json (declared model and sampling metadata, temperature = null), deterministic_reconciliation.json (provider-call audit), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, and representative validator traces under execution/scoring/*. No human manual manuscript editing or content insertion occurred after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit under the shared_initial_candidate contract.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per‑condition generation, multi‑sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single‑model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling‑parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (sampling parameters unset); null indicates provider default sampling semantics determined runtime sampling behavior and is residual uncertainty recorded in the archived configuration.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact‑match checks were applied, but private training‑data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
